newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel expects better job market, economy in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Waigel expects better job market, economy in 1998.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday he expected Germany's economy and labour market to improve in 1998, enabling the country to clearly undershoot the deficit goal of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1998 for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"We will be in a better situation next year. The prospects for growth are better and jobless levels will fall," Waigel said.
"The deficit will be clearly below three percent (of GDP)," he said. Waigel had said earlier that the 1998 deficit would be a "sufficient margin" below three percent.
Waigel declined comment on foreign exchange markets.
The dollar has been lingering near a six-year high against the mark.
"I will not make daily statements (on the dollar)," he said.
He also declined to comment on France's audit of public finances next week, which is expected to show France's deficit has strayed well beyond the EMU target .
"The French government will make a decision. I think I'll leave that to the French," Waigel said.
